spatial_claims.claim: AB is a given finite straight line
C is a point on segment AB between A and B, constructed by Proposition 2.11 such that rect(AB, CB) = sq(AC)
AB, AC, CB are three straight lines (C divides AB into two sub-segments)
AC is the greater segment and CB is the lesser segment of AB

configuration_map: Point C: Constructed on segment AB via Proposition 2.11. Lies between A and B, dividing AB into two segments: AC (the greater segment, from A to C) and CB (the lesser segment, from C to B). The relation rect(AB, CB) = sq(AC) holds by construction. C maintains a consistent position on AB throughout all steps. No other auxiliary points or figures are constructed.
pass_reason: The proof makes minimal spatial claims -- only that C is a point on segment AB between A and B. All subsequent reasoning is algebraic/proportional (applying 6.17 converse to derive the proportion AB:AC = AC:CB from rect(AB, CB) = sq(AC)). There are no angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, no ray orderings, and no circle arguments. The few spatial claims present are mutually consistent.
